matrixSearch.notes: Official allergen material was found. It is an absence/modification guide rather than a positive contains matrix. Direct ingredient positives come only from current restaurant-issued or linked-vendor descriptions; empty/absence codes are not treated as proof of a product being allergen-free.

restaurantLevelAllergenEvidence.text: China Chilcano states that normal kitchen operations use shared cooking surfaces, utensils and common fryer oil, so menu items may contact allergens. This remains restaurant-level evidence and is not smeared into item-specific may-contain fields.
China Chilcano says it cannot guarantee any menu item is entirely free of nut allergens. This remains a restaurant-level limitation, not an item-specific contains or may-contain claim.

findings.summary: The 56-row baseline omits current lunch, brunch, nonalcoholic, package and seasonal products and includes alcohol-only/tasting-component artifacts plus stale desserts.
The official Allergy Menu PDF letters mean prepared without or can be prepared without; treating those letters as positive contains claims would invert the restaurant disclosure.
The restaurant explicitly discloses shared surfaces, utensils and fryer oil and cannot guarantee any item entirely free of nut allergens.

Several baseline positives rely on culinary inference from mayo, buns, dumplings or absent-guide codes; the proposal keeps only literal current ingredient positives and stores shared-kitchen language at restaurant level.

proposedChanges: Replace the 56-row partial projection with the 82-product consolidated union of six official menu tabs, linked Toast food/NA offerings, and the current rotating Ceviche Fest special.
Collapse repeated service-period presentations; remove alcohol-only, stale dessert and tasting-component artifacts while retaining the two actual chef tasting menus.
Preserve only literal direct ingredient positives; do not invert the official allergy-guide absence codes or infer positives from culinary expectations.
Retain shared-surface, utensil, common-fryer and no-guaranteed-nut-free language at restaurant level without item-level may-contain smear.
